---
title: "Normal Approximation"
description: >-
  This is a statistical tutorial demonstrating when the normal distribution can
  approximate a binomial distribution.
categories: [Tutorial, Stats, Distribution]
jupyter: main
---

```{python}
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
from scipy.stats import binom, hypergeom, norm

import sys
print(sys.executable)
print(sys.version)
```

```{python}
def compare_normal_approx(n, p, title):
    """Compare binomial distribution with its normal approximation."""
    mu = n * p
    sigma = np.sqrt(n * p * (1 - p))

    # Exact binomial PMF
    k = np.arange(0, n + 1)
    pmf = binom.pmf(k, n, p)

    # Normal approximation (with continuity correction for the demo below)
    x = np.linspace(max(0, mu - 4*sigma), mu + 4*sigma, 500)
    pdf = norm.pdf(x, mu, sigma)

    # Plot
    plt.figure(figsize=(8, 4))
    plt.bar(k, pmf, alpha=0.6, label=f"Binomial(n={n}, p={p})")
    plt.plot(x, pdf, "r-", lw=2, label=f"Normal(μ={mu:.1f}, σ={sigma:.2f})")
    plt.title(title)
    plt.xlabel("k")
    plt.ylabel("Probability")
    plt.legend()
    plt.tight_layout()

    # Numeric check: P(X <= some value), exact vs normal approx
    k0 = int(mu)  # P(X <= np)
    exact = binom.cdf(k0, n, p)
    approx_no_cc = norm.cdf(k0, mu, sigma)
    approx_cc = norm.cdf(k0 + 0.5, mu, sigma)  # continuity correction

# Case 1: np < 5  -> approximation is POOR
compare_normal_approx(20, 0.1, "Case 1: np = 2 < 5 (approximation fails)")

# Case 2: np > 5 and n(1-p) > 5 -> approximation is GOOD
compare_normal_approx(400, 0.05, "Case 2: np = 20, n(1-p) = 380 (approximation works)")

plt.show()

```
